Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Notice has been served on the informant through learned A.G.A.
This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the anticipatory bail rejection order dated 27.10.2023 while rejecting the anticipatory bail of the appellant in Complaint Case No. 91 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(s) S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Bachrayu, District Amroha.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the present criminal appeal has been filed by the appellant against the order passed in anticipatory bail application while rejecting the application.

Since the appellant also belonged to S.C./S.T. caste, therefore, offence under S.C/S.T.
Act cannot be said to be made out.
The appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed the present offence.

Further submitted that in this case, occurrence is said to have taken place on 25.9.2021 regarding which an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed in which order was passed by the learned court to register the case as a result F.I.R. was lodged on 10.1.2022.
After investigation no any occurrence was found to be established, therefore, final report was filed by the police.

Protest was filed before the learned court by the informant/victim which was treated as complaint and after recording he statement of the victim/witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C, summoning order was passed against the appellant and other co-accused persons under Section 376-D, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)Dha S.C./S.T.
It is also submitted that allegations made in the F.I.R. and protest are totally false and no such incident took place at all.

The fact is that the father of the appellant Brahmpal filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. before the learned court on 24.8.2021 for committing gang rape with her daughter in which the husband of the informant was also made an accused which was treated as complaint and summoning order was passed by the learned court concerned.

In counterblast for making pressure on the appellant,
present application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed by the present informant, wife of Babloo who was made an accused in the previous complaint lodged by the father of the appellant.
Present application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed by the informant, subsequent to the application filed by the father of the appellant.
In this way, there is no any other material on record to show the complicity of the appellant in the present case.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
There is no criminal antecedent against him.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the anticipatory bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

On the other hand, learned AGA opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and contended that there is allegation on the part of the informant and witnesses from which a prima facie case is made out against him but could not dispute that the appellant belongs to S.C./S.T. caste.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. perusal of record, since the appellant himself belongs to S.C./S.T.
Caste by which bar under Section 18 of the Act cannot be said to be applicable in this case, there appears ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the appellant during pendency of trial.
The Court below erred in rejecting the anticipatory bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the anticipatory bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

sentences.text: Let the appellantRahul involved inComplaint Case No. 91 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(s) S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Bachrayu, District Amroha be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 16.1.2024 Anurag Singh  Rahul vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21163581/
